name: The Shared Eighty
description: Named home for the archetype objects type-bundles compose from. Laws encoded: §0.2 R7 corollary (a new hosting type reuses >=80% known objects; genuinely-distinct stays <=20%) and §4.10 authoring rule 'skin the mechanics, never skin the silhouette' (R61: reserve the ~15 genuinely-distinct verb-changing objects game-wide; everything else is a costume on a shared-mechanics object). Both shipped prototype-anchor bundles (official:shared-web, official:game-servers) point buildables.paletteRef here; every archetype their buildables.archetypeInstances name MUST be defined in this file — the content validator makes a dangling paletteRef or an unknown archetype loud red (audit group-13: the ref previously resolved nowhere).

archetypes.object: The countable concurrency pool — slots that fill, a queue that backs up, patience that drains (§4.10 names it as ONE object wearing five costumes).
costumes: shared-web: the per-account connection-slot pool (the oversell ratio rides this same object)
game-servers: the game-server slot (tick-budgeted sessions in rooms)
future: the serverless warm pool — cross-reference verbChangerReserve item 'warm-pool'

archetypes.object: The rack vessel with an authored front and an authored back — two-face law, G6 (the back view is canonical for rack verbs).
archetypes.engine: sim-core topology rack grid + blast-radius projection (packages/sim-core/src/topology/)
costumes: game-servers: the tick-node rack row behind the inspector's metronome panel

archetypes.object: The panel the customer lives in — a cPanel-class god view over one account's slice.
The session rendezvous object that projects players into rooms — a genuine verb-changer occupying an archetype slot (§4.10 names it in the R61 reserve).
archetypes.engine: waves arrival routing + the game-servers 'matchmaker-projection' mechanic (packages/sim-core/src/waves/)
costumes: game-servers: the server-browser matchmaking tier (archetypeInstance skin 'game-servers')

verbChangerReserve.source: hosting_game.md §4.10 / R61 — the ~15 genuinely-distinct, verb-changing objects reserved for the whole game. The accounting lives in this palette so a content lane cannot silently spend the reserve: the validator fails when items exceed max or when a palette archetype marked verbChanger is absent from this list.

openQuestions: The full >=80% common-object catalogue beyond these four engine-backed archetypes is future Phase-2 content (audit group-13 finding: named per-tier buildables had no home; this palette is the home, its shelves beyond the archetype layer await authoring).

The per-bundle 20% distinct-budget arithmetic is not machine-enforced yet: bundle distinct lists (shared-web 12+3, game-servers 8+3) are hand-reviewed against §0.2 R7 until the common catalogue is large enough for the ratio to mean anything.
